To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the optic disc is a dynamic structure that changes in size during development; 2) the normal human optic disc has a characteristic shape that can be described by the parameters of an ellipse; and 3) the optic disc shape can be used to identify developmental abnormalities.

(i) the optic disc is a complex structure that develops in the context of multiple genetic, environmental and epigenetic influences, (ii) optic disc anomalies are common, (iii) optic disc anomalies can be associated with systemic disease, (iv) the pathogenesis of optic nerve hypoplasia and other optic disc anomalies is complex and incompletely understood.

1) the developmental anomalies arising from defective fissure closure are associated with a range of systemic abnormalities; 2) the optic-disc anomalies that are associated with systemic abnormalities include those arising from defects of ganglion-cell development, and some of the optic-disc anomalies associated with systemic abnormalities are not associated with developmental anomalies of the optic-nerve fibres.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the optic nerve, the optic disc and the visual pathway.
the development of the optic nerve
the developmental biology of the human eye, the causes of visual loss, the development of novel therapies and the development of novel diagnostic techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optic disc is a complex structure with many potential developmental abnormalities, which can occur in isolation or in combination with other anomalies.
the optic disc is a highly variable structure in terms of its size, shape, and colour. This is because of the complex development of this area of the eye,
the developmental optic-disc anomalies are a heterogeneous group of abnormalities that can arise from a variety of causes, and that the clinical features and systemic associations are often subtle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most important and most common developmental anomalies of the optic-nerve head are those associated with the development of the optic fissure, and the most important of these is the coloboma of the optic disc, which is often associated with systemic malformations.
the development of the optic nerve is complex, involving multiple genes, and that the optic nerve and the brain have common developmental origins.
developmental abnormalities of the optic disc and nerve are important causes of visual impairment and blindness, and are often associated with other systemic abnormalities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the clinical presentation of optic-nerve developmental abnormalities is extremely variable, but the underlying pathology is often the same, and that a high degree of suspicion is needed to make the diagnosis.
the optic-nerve defects are not isolated, but part of a spectrum of developmental anomalies.

developmental anomalies of the optic disc are a significant cause of childhood blindness and visual disability, and that they are often associated not only with systemic abnormalities but also with other ocular abnormalities that are important in the clinical management of the patient and in the genetic analysis.
